evangelism.share: up to 75% of expenses for a full-message reaping series (15+ meetings); the church pays at least 25%
evangelism.cap: $18,000 per church district (full series by an NPUC or NAD guest evangelist; citywide campaigns excepted); $10,500 per district (full series by an Alaska pastor); $1,000 (partial series of 7–14 days, one per church per event); $500 (series under 7 days)

conditions: Evangelism funds are for reaping series only, not sowing or nurturing events.
A full-message series is 15 or more continuous meetings covering all the church's major doctrines; 14 or fewer meetings, or any ShareHIM series, counts as partial.
The budget lists the church contribution, meeting offerings and conference assistance.
The local church treasurer handles the money, never mixed with personal funds; offerings are deposited as received and listed separately; every expense needs a receipt or voucher.
Apart from the advance, money is paid only on receipts; any balance goes back to the conference with the final report.
Bible worker subsidy: up to $500 a month for up to 3 months before and during a full-message series by an approved NPUC or NAD evangelist (prioritised by available funds).
Equipment subsidy: $500 (one series a year) for a pastor or administrator who conducts a full-message series of 15+ meetings, approved before it starts, paid on receipts.
evangelism.report: Income and expense report on treasury forms, with receipts, within 30 days after the meetings close; any balance returned. Media-ministry interests are followed up and reported on the monthly Pastor's Report.

evangelism.share: not a fixed share: the church is encouraged to cover at least 50% of a large-scale reaping series, and 25–50% of other approaches

conditions: Select at least one desired outcome to qualify: new interests added to a database, appeals for Bible studies, or appeals for baptism.
A reaping event is planned as a six-phase evangelism cycle: Revitalize (7–8 months before), Fertilize (5–6 months), Sow (3–4 months), Grow (1–2 months), Reap, Keep (1–3 months after).
Large-scale reaping series: usually 3–6 weeks with an in-person evangelist. Small-scale: usually under 3 weeks, in person or online/downlink, with more pre-work.
The budget lists church contribution and requested conference contribution; total income should cover expenses.

evangelism.how: Send the UCC Evangelism/Outreach Subsidy Request (next year's plans plus a review of last year) and the Evangelism Budget Request to the Ministerial Department. The evangelism/outreach allocation committee sets the amount.
conditions: The allocation committee weighs the total evangelism funds available for the year, amounts designated for population centres, and the church's total and per-capita tithe.
Money must be used for outreach-oriented activities and events. Sowing and reaping are subsidised; discipling is listed as non-subsidised.

Information asked: outreach plans with budget for each church, three years of tithe, baptism and attendance figures, a review of last year's plans, whether a conference-sponsored Bible instructor is wanted, and how many members are in ministry.
Budget form income lines: offerings, local church(es), request from conference. It is approved by the UCC Evangelism Coordinator.
Pastor's equipment (2021 memo): $1,000 after the pastor's own series of at least 15 presentations (UCC $500 + NPUC $500), with reports.
evangelism.report: UCC Evangelistic Report after each series: subsidy, church contribution, expenses and how any balance is budgeted; outreach team and Bible worker use; visitors, baptisms, professions of faith, rebaptisms, commitments, Bible studies and interests. Receipts go to the local church treasurer for the church audit.
programmes: Serve One More: the conference provides ideas, funding and support for churches serving their communities (2026)
Hispanic evangelistic caravan 'Try with Jesus', 17–25 April 2026, nine locations, 240+ baptisms; another caravan planned for 2027
Strategic Plan 2023–2025: a UCC-wide evangelistic thrust by 31 December 2025, a new urban center of influence and a Next Generation church plant

NPUC Evangelistic Allowance (union level): $1,500 for a pastor who conducts or hosts a full-message evangelistic meeting ($750 NPUC + $750 conference); the conference's own programme sets what qualifies; limited number, first come first served; send the form and a 250–500-word story to the conference evangelism/ministerial department after the meetings

childProtection.conference: Adventist Screening Verification (Sterling Volunteers) is mandatory for all adults over 18 in any capacity in children's and youth ministries, and for all church ministry leaders and officers voted or appointed by the local church. Volunteers give four references, one of them a pastor or other mandatory reporter, and no relatives. The conference screening coordinator rates each volunteer Level 1–3, and each church appoints a Local Volunteer Screening Coordinator. New and renewing volunteers give references, but the renewal period is not stated.

evangelism.how: Plan a 12–18-month cycle of evangelism with the conference's Revangelism team (book a church growth consultation). Use the conference budget sheet, which has a church-board approval date and 'Local Church Contribution' and 'Conference Contribution' lines.
conditions: The conference budget sets aside money for evangelistic series, discipleship programmes, church plants and personal witnessing training (about $700,000 in all, with the annual evangelism offering).

Pastor's choice of an equipment subsidy (up to $750) or a $500 bonus: hold at least one full-message campaign of at least 15 presentations (3+ nights a week) in the same year the equipment was bought; include a story and pictures; equipment bought with your own funds becomes your property; receipts required.
Eligible equipment: laptops, printers, video projectors, digital art, evangelistic sermons, iPads/iPods, software, sound systems.
evangelism.report: No post-meeting report is published for conference evangelism funds. The equipment/bonus request asks for a story, pictures and receipts, and the NPUC allowance asks for a 250–500-word story after the meetings.
